::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at Part 3](../../slides/cohabitation-one-day.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The second stage of the case, about six hours of work, takes three tasks, and it begins with the reproduction, before any other page of the case is opened. Task 3 reproduces a test that Multi100 recorded for one of the five analysts and then asks what the number rests on. The answer is the main lesson of the case, and you find it in the counts. The second part of the task refits the published coefficient from the survey itself. Once Task 3 is done, the reading order of stage 8 no longer applies, and the rest of the stage opens the menu, the curve, and the later sections of the case study and of the event-history module.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, Part 3 as far as its two hands-on slides, and Task 3 in your report or working script, or [browser lab](../../cases/cohabitation/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) Task 3 | The instruction of Task 2 of Multi100 and the aim of the reproduction. Then `check_score_file()` confirms that `data/score_person_months.csv` is the file that the analysts received, and the chunk of Task 3, the code of analyst 5X3KG, compares the share of person-month rows that record a marriage in the 1995 survey with the share in the survey of 2006–2010. It gives $\chi^2(1)$ = 47.474 on 23,949 rows, the value that Multi100 recorded for 5X3KG, and `prep/reproduce_5X3KG.R` holds every step as a script. Read the shares behind the test, then find out what they rest on: count the unions of the file, one row per woman, and set the 1995 cohort beside the 929 unions of the paper. Finally, `fit_spec(unions, adjust = "race_period")` refits Model 2 of the paper on the rebuilt unions: −0.686 (SE 0.138) against the published −0.683 (0.14). The workspace reproduces this one analyst, and the browser lab runs the same reproduction live. | 60 minutes |
| Slides, the rest of Part 3, from [the file and the rebuild](../../slides/cohabitation-one-day.html#/the-file-and-the-rebuild){target="_blank"} | The file of the analysts set beside the rebuild of the course, the five analyses on a repaired file, and what a reproduction does and does not establish; what the published coefficient means beside an interaction of race-ethnicity and period, and why the reference specification of the course, −0.730, leaves the interaction out; then the menu, weights and the design of the survey, the length of the whole union, and the discrete-time models. | 35 minutes |
| [Case study](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd#sec-reanalysts), from section 3 to section 6 | The five reanalyses, the file of the analysts and how its rows were built, the rebuild of the course, what a reproduction establishes, [the replications](../../cases/cohabitation/index.qmd#sec-replication), and the results of the paper and the analysts on one scale. | 45 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/cohabitation/menu.qmd), and Task 4 in your report or working script | The fifteen decisions at three levels, the six on which the curve keeps more than one option, and the 144 specifications that they make. Then `try_spec()` with no arguments and three or four times more, one argument at a time, compared with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for `histories = "score_file"` to read why it is refused, and send the try that you would defend with `submit_exploration()` if you want it on the [class chart](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd#class-results). | 40 minutes |
| Slides, [Part 4](../../slides/cohabitation-one-day.html#/part-4-multiverse-replication-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} | The class chart against the curve of 144, what moved the estimate, the cohort window that carries most of its variance, and the two replications of the paper, which tested two different coefficients. The critics of the multiverse and the slides on the archive repeat stage 4; skip them. | 20 minutes |
| The preregistration block in your report | Complete the block before you run anything: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, one option for each of the fifteen decisions, a sentence from your causal graph on why the specification answers the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Render the report and keep the rendered copy, then fit the specification with `run_spec()`, and send it with `report_result()` if you want it on the chart. | 25 minutes |
| [Event-history analysis](../../companion/event-history.qmd), from [Person-period data](../../companion/event-history.qmd#sec-person-period) to [Period and cohort](../../companion/event-history.qmd#sec-period-cohort) | Person-period data; the discrete-time logit and the baseline of time since the start; the complementary log-log model, the version of the proportional hazards model for time measured in whole months; competing risks with a multinomial logit, the model of the paper; and period against cohort. | 75 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/cohabitation/multiverse.qmd) | Reading the curve, the reference marks, what moved the estimate, inference with design-based errors, and the displays beside the curve: the life table, marriage within three years, the groups behind the claim, and other surveys. | 30 minutes |
| Your report | Render the report with all five tasks complete, the preregistration as it stood before the run and the result beneath it. This is the third case report. | 20 minutes |

**Shortcuts.** If the discrete-time models are familiar, read only the section of the event-history module on [competing risks](../../companion/event-history.qmd#sec-competing), which is the model of the paper.

**By the end of the stage** you have reproduced $\chi^2(1)$ = 47.474 yourself and found out what the file behind it holds, refitted the published coefficient from the survey and can say whose change it measures, declared and run one specification of the curve of 144, and rendered the third case report.
